question: After the concrete defects are fixed, should Crabbox accept CUA’s credentialed alpha-SDK subprocess and destructive remote lifecycle as a built-in provider contract?
rationale: Mechanical repairs cannot determine whether this permanent trust, dependency, ownership, and deletion boundary belongs in Crabbox core.

options.title: Repair then reassess built-in support
options.body: Require all safety fixes, a current-main refresh, fresh exact-head CI, and credentialed live proof before final built-in acceptance.

options.title: Narrow to non-destructive support
options.body: Limit the contribution to doctor or explicitly experimental non-destructive behavior until lifecycle ownership matures.

options.title: Defer CUA integration
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/381 open for later but stop treating this branch as a current landing candidate.

recommendation.title: Repair then reassess built-in support
recommendation.body: Require all safety fixes, a current-main refresh, fresh exact-head CI, and credentialed live proof before final built-in acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across the current delegated-run framework and this PR’s identity and cleanup hardening.
